stemMd: Equal volumes of 0.10 mol L⁻¹ HCl and 0.10 mol L⁻¹ NaOH are mixed at 25 °C. Assume complete dissociation and no other solutes. What is the approximate final pH?
explanationMd: Equal volumes and equal concentrations provide equal moles of H⁺ and OH⁻. They react in a one-to-one ratio to form water, leaving a solution of sodium chloride with no stoichiometric acid or base excess. At 25 °C the idealized solution is approximately neutral, pH 7.

distractorRationale.a: This ignores neutralization by an equal amount of strong base.
distractorRationale.d: This ignores the equal amount of strong acid.
distractorRationale.b: Dilution alone is not the main event because acid and base react.
distractorRationale.e: There is no excess hydroxide after equal mole amounts react.
